# Native block registry, metadata 0

`block-registry-meta0.tsv` is generated by `BlockRegistryOracle` from the pinned
Beta 1.7.3 client. It lists every non-null `uu.m` entry in ID order, the runtime
class and its SHA-256, `b()` render type, `c()` opacity, whether the runtime
class overrides the world-aware face-texture method, and six calls to that method
for faces 0..5. The header pins the JAR and `uu`, `xp`, and `ln` class hashes.
The oracle validates the JAR and class origin before calling client methods.

The synthetic `xp` world is shared with `ViewOracle`: metadata 0, air above,
non-opaque neighbours, other integer/boolean queries zero/false and floating
queries 1. Override-marked rows may change in other worlds; even unmarked rows
are not evidence for other metadata, geometry, alpha, face visibility or runtime
state. These observations do not alone establish support in the renderer.

Reproduce (from the worktree root):

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/block-registry-oracle
javac -cp ../.local/minecraft/client-b1.7.3.jar -d /tmp/block-registry-oracle tools/oracle/src/ViewOracle.java tools/oracle/src/BlockRegistryOracle.java
java -cp /tmp/block-registry-oracle:../.local/minecraft/client-b1.7.3.jar BlockRegistryOracle ../.local/minecraft/client-b1.7.3.jar
python3 -m unittest tests.python.test_block_registry_oracle -v
```

The audit skips live reproduction if the local JAR or Java tools are missing;
a wrong JAR or any byte difference fails it.

`block-cubes-meta0.tsv` is generated by `BlockCubeOracle` for the fourteen added
viewer mappings. It additionally captures six bounds coordinates, all terrain
tile alpha masks, and native visibility in each direction against stone and
all fourteen added IDs. The oracle verifies JAR and terrain SHA-256 and records
hashes of `uu`, `xp`, and `ln`; it requires inherited world texture, bounds update, and visibility methods, and records concrete class hashes. It also verifies the six textures for all metadata values match metadata 0. Pair visibility is represented in ID order 4, 5, 22, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 57, 58, 80, 82, 87, 89, with six
face bits per pair. This covers metadata 0 and the synthetic world described
above, rather than arbitrary neighbor classes or metadata.

```sh
javac -cp ../.local/minecraft/client-b1.7.3.jar -d /tmp/block-registry-oracle tools/oracle/src/ViewOracle.java tools/oracle/src/BlockCubeOracle.java
java -cp /tmp/block-registry-oracle:../.local/minecraft/client-b1.7.3.jar BlockCubeOracle ../.local/minecraft/client-b1.7.3.jar ../.local/minecraft/terrain.png
```

`block-metadata-cubes.tsv` is generated by `BlockMetadataCubeOracle` for log
(ID 17) and wool (ID 35), for each metadata nibble 0..15. It pins JAR,
terrain, base and concrete classes; captures native bounds, texture and alpha
on all six faces, and both visibility directions with stone. It verifies the
world-aware texture, bounds update and visibility methods are inherited from
`uu`. These cases do not establish unrelated game behavior for those blocks.
The Python audit compiles the oracle and reproduces its output twice.
